newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra posts chunky 1996 profit jump.
newsitem.headline: Astra posts chunky 1996 profit jump.

text.p: Swedish pharmaceutical company Astra AB said on Wednesday its 1996 earnings rose 10 percent and profited from the occasion by announcing a stock dividend, a share split and a higher dividend.

Astra, whose main products are anti-ulcer drug Losec and asthma medicine Pulmicort, said its Losec sales jumped 23 percent in the year. Pre-tax profit totalled 13.22 billion crowns ($1.8 billion) on sales of 38.99 billion crowns.
The board of directors proposed a one for three stock dividend and a two for one stock split.
"This is a way to turn balance sheet profits to share capital...we think shareholders will welcome the free shares," Astra spokesman Steffan Ternby told Reuters.
Sales of Astra's blockbusting anti-ulcer drug Losec rose 23 percent, calculated at constant exchange rates, to 17.56 billion crowns. Otherwise the increase was 15 percent.
Total Losec sales worldwide amounted to 24.63 billion crowns, up from 21.0 billion in the previous year.
"Losec thereby became the top selling pharmaceutical in the world in 1996," Astra said in a statement.
"It was a good report, in line with expectations," said analyst Goran Kallebo from Matteus.
"Astra's own Losec sales were excellent. Only the pain control area was a little lower than expected," Kallebo said.
The stock split news had no effect on the share, he said.
Sales of the anti-asthma agent Pulmicort rose to 4.73 billion crowns from 4.34 billion, a 17 percent rise calculated at constant exchange rates.

Sales of beta-blocker Seloken were growing rapidly, the company said. "This is mainly due to a favourable trend in the U.S., where the product is marketed by Astra USA under the name Toprol-XL," Astra said.
Total sales of Seloken rose to 2.60 billion crowns from 2.43 billion, it said. Sales of vasodilator Plendil rose to 1.94 billion crowns from 1.69 billion.
Sales in the pain control group totalled 3.34 compared to 3.48 billion crowns, Astra said.
straa.

North American sales rose to 10.31 billion crowns from 8.40 billion, of which Astra's share in its half-owned Astra Merck, Inc. accounted for 6.00 billion crowns compared to 4.59 billion a year earlier.
Sales in its wholly owned subsidiary Astra USA Inc. rose to 2.65 billion crowns from 2.33 billion.
"At constant exchange rates, sales growth in North American was 30 percent," Astra said in a statement.
Sales in Europe at constant exchange rates rose 12 percent to 22.48 billion crowns.
It said growth in the fourth quarter was 19 percent or 21 percent with exchange rate movements taken into account.
Astra said the Swedish market was affected in the last two months of the year because of patient hoarding prior to changes in drug payment compensation which took effect on January 1, 1997.
-- Abigail Schmelz, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1003
